articles.originalTitle: Best Building Envelope & Cladding Products of 2026 - Architectural Record
articles.title: The Best Building Envelope and Cladding Products of 2026
articles.excerpt: The top building envelope and cladding products for 2026 highlight advancements in thermal performance, sustainable harvesting, and innovative material technologies.
articles.content: The top building envelope and cladding products for 2026 showcase innovative materials and enhanced performance standards across architecture. Arktura expanded its Vapor collection with perforated aluminum panels suitable for exterior applications, offering multiple sizes, patterns, and powder-coat finishes. The exoTHERM system provides an adjustable fiber-reinforced polymer bracket designed for ventilated rainscreen facades, offering thermal isolation. Sustainably harvested Japanese cedar CVG Sugi features a tight vertical grain with high dimensional stability. Sicaro, a fortified radiata pine plank, utilizes a proprietary water-based treatment to enhance durability and comes with a 55-year above-ground warranty. The Lunawood 2026 collection, recognized as best in category, introduces thermally modified timber options with 11 new finishes and an ignition-resistant Class A rating. Kingspan's Kooltherm K100 series delivers high thermal performance in thin assemblies, while Carlisle Syntech's ThermaThin roof insulation board incorporates up to 34% recycled content. Additionally, BÖK Modern introduced Simple Mount Sunshades, bracketless shades that attach directly outside the window flange for streamlined installation.

articles.originalTitle: How Frieze became the latest step in Abu Dhabi's cultural masterplan - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Frieze Fair Launches as the Latest Step in Abu Dhabi Cultural Masterplan
articles.excerpt: The inaugural Frieze Abu Dhabi fair opens at Manarat Al Saadiyat on Saadiyat Island, seeking to promote regional artists and position the city as a destination for international collectors.
articles.content: Building on over two decades of cultural development in the United Arab Emirates, Frieze is launching its first Middle East fair in Abu Dhabi. Running from November 19 to 22 at Manarat Al Saadiyat, the inaugural Frieze Abu Dhabi is held in partnership with Abu Dhabi's Department of Culture and Tourism. The emirate's art fair originated in 2007 as ArtParis Abu Dhabi before rebranding as Abu Dhabi Art and moving to Saadiyat Island. Over time, the focus shifted from heavy reliance on Western blue-chip galleries toward stronger representation of the Arab region and the Global South. Sustained efforts by regional galleries have increased the institutional backing and international recognition for art from the Arab world. Directed by Dyala Nusseibeh, the fair aims to integrate the regional market more closely into the global art network. The launch coincides with broader cultural developments in the emirate, including the forthcoming Guggenheim Abu Dhabi and other museums in the Saadiyat Cultural District. Frieze's parent company, Mari, maintains financial backing linked to Abu Dhabi through strategic investors such as the sovereign wealth fund Mubadala. The partnership aligns with Abu Dhabi's wider strategy to establish itself as a prominent destination for international cultural events and global elites.

articles.originalTitle: How Does an Artist Know When She’s Done? A Major Marisa Merz Retrospective Turns the Question on Its Head - ARTnews.com
articles.title: Marisa Merz Retrospective in Turin Explores the Artist's Life and Work
articles.excerpt: Marking the centenary of her birth, a comprehensive retrospective exhibition across three institutions in Turin explores Italian artist Marisa Merz's five-decade artistic output.
articles.content: Marking the centenary of the birth of Italian artist Marisa Merz, a comprehensive retrospective titled "Marisa Merz: La danza delle ore (The Dance of the Hours)" has opened across three institutions in Turin. The exhibition is hosted by the Galleria d’Arte Moderna e Contemporanea Torino, the Fondazione Merz, and the Castello di Rivoli. As the only woman affiliated with the Arte Povera movement, Merz became known for her incorporation of domestic labor and nontraditional media. Born in Turin in 1926, the artist was famously camera-shy and rarely titled or dated her compositions. Honored with a Golden Lion at the Venice Biennale in 2013, her retrospective deliberately avoids a chronological itinerary. Curators have displayed provisional works straight from the studio, complete with tacked notes and Post-its. Tacita Dean was also commissioned to produce a 16 mm film diptych and photographs capturing Merz's apartment and studio. Additionally, the exhibition stages encounters between Merz and contemporary women artists such as Leonor Antunes, Thea Djordjadze, and Miriam Cahn. Merz passed away in 2019.

articles.originalTitle: Eight Dead, 18 Injured in Brooklyn Building Collapse Next to Construction Site - Engineering News-Record
articles.title: Eight Dead After Brooklyn Building Collapses Next to Excavation Site
articles.excerpt: A 96-year-old building in Brooklyn collapsed into an adjoining excavation site, resulting in eight deaths and 18 injuries. Official investigations into the incident are currently underway.
articles.content: An adjoining three-story building collapsed into an excavation site in Brooklyn on November 11, killing eight people, including two children and two construction workers, and injuring 18 others. Fire department rescue operations concluded on November 12. Project geotechnical and engineering records indicated that abutting structures required underpinning and warned that excavation vibration could adversely affect adjacent properties. A preconstruction survey conducted on March 5 had documented visible cracking and rated the masonry facades poorly. Following the collapse, the mayor ordered safety inspections at approximately 100 other construction sites linked to the project's firms, while both the New York Attorney General and the Brooklyn District Attorney initiated separate investigations. City records show the development had faced prior stop-work orders during earlier demolition phases before corrections allowed work to resume. The exact cause of the structural failure remains under investigation by municipal authorities.

articles.originalTitle: Designers’ Creative Freedom Unveiled at Molteni Museum Exhibit - WWD
articles.title: Molteni Museum Exhibition Grants Designers Creative Freedom Beyond Commercial Constraints
articles.excerpt: A new exhibition at the Molteni Museum in Giussano allows prominent designers to reinterpret existing furniture pieces without commercial and engineering constraints.
articles.content: Hosted at the Molteni Compound in Giussano, Italy, the Molteni Museum has launched a new exhibition designed to offer furniture designers rare creative freedom, unhindered by commercial and engineering pressures. Conceived with artist Ron Gilad, the project highlights living creatives by utilizing existing pieces from Molteni Group brands as the foundation for expressive, one-of-a-kind works. The exhibition features contributions from internationally recognized practices and designers, including Herzog & de Meuron, Jean Nouvel, Naoto Fukasawa, OMA, AMDL Circle, Foster + Partners Industrial Design, Patricia Urquiola, the late Luca Meda, and Vincent Van Duysen. Participants explored material experimentation and playful concepts without traditional constraints. Herzog & de Meuron incorporated inflatable cushions into a special-edition chair, while OMA and AMDL Circle applied surreal material interpretations to established collections. Gilad contributed a fountain as a tribute to Luca Meda's kitchen design. Accompanied by video installations by Muse Factory of Projects documenting the manufacturing and research processes, the exhibition will remain on display for one year before embarking on a global tour across a yet-to-be-determined roster of cities.

articles.originalTitle: Berkshire Glade by Turkel Design - Architectural Record
articles.title: Turkel Design Completes Berkshire Glade Residence in Western Massachusetts
articles.excerpt: Situated in the Berkshire hills of Western Massachusetts, Berkshire Glade by Turkel Design functions as a multigenerational vacation home and future full-time residence. The 6,510-square-foot property comprises two distinct volumes joined by a covered porch.
articles.content:
Designed by Turkel Design, Berkshire Glade is located in the Berkshire hills of Western Massachusetts and overlooks a tree-lined hillside with views of Mount Washington. Spanning 6,510 square feet, the property serves as both a multigenerational vacation home and a future full-time residence for a couple whose careers span New York City and Boston.

The residential project consists of two distinct volumes, a primary residence and a guest house, joined by a covered porch anchored by a fireplace. The engineered-wood structure utilizes natural materials including Douglas fir glue-laminated beams and thermally modified hemlock. The exterior is clad in shou sugi ban, a Japanese charred wood resistant to rot and insects. Components including exterior and interior wall systems, roof and floor systems, windows, doors, flooring, and custom built-in cabinetry were fabricated as a package in a climate-controlled facility before being shipped to the site for precision assembly. The project was completed in May 2025.

articles.originalTitle: Crosslam completes Brazil’s tallest mass-timber tower - Dezeen
articles.title: Brazil's Tallest Mass-Timber Hybrid Tower Completed in São Paulo
articles.excerpt: Engineering firm Crosslam has completed Aurora 275, a hybrid timber building in São Paulo that is the tallest of its type in Brazil. Standing 22 meters tall, the structure was built to demonstrate mass-timber potential to the local market.
articles.content: Engineering firm Crosslam has designed and built Aurora 275, a hybrid timber building located in the Suzano area of São Paulo, which the company states is the tallest of its type in Brazil. Standing 22 meters tall, Aurora 275 features a structural system consisting of a reinforced concrete core, metal elements, and mass-timber components including glulam beams and columns and cross-laminated timber floorplates. Crosslam, which typically acts as an engineer for other firms, designed the building to demonstrate the viability of mass timber and build trust within the Brazilian market. Constructed in four weeks by a five-person team, the building utilizes timber sourced within Brazil. The structure features a metal-clad facade with yellow detailing and includes balconies for its 10 apartments. Interior spaces expose the timber elements to provide a warm aesthetic. According to the project team, engineered timber offers construction advantages such as faster assembly, dimensional precision, reduced site waste, a lighter structure, and lower carbon emissions. The company claimed the building is carbon neutral.

articles.originalTitle: SITE Santa Fe Announces Theme and Artist List for 13th International Biennial - ARTnews.com
articles.title: SITE Santa Fe Announces Theme and Artist List for 13th Biennial
articles.excerpt: Ekow Eshun will curate the 13th International Biennial at SITE Santa Fe, opening next June. Titled "There Are Other Worlds," the exhibition will feature more than 40 artists.
articles.content: SITE Santa Fe in New Mexico has announced the theme and artist list for its 13th International Biennial, opening next June. Exhibition curator Ekow Eshun selected the title "There Are Other Worlds," a release stated, positing that other worlds already exist within our own through plain sight, refusal of the status quo, or imagination. The exhibition comprises 3 sections: "Worlds Beyond," informed in part by the Transcendental Painting Group; "World in Common," examining community and kinship; and "Worlds Alive," focusing on human, animal, and plant interdependence. More than 40 artists will exhibit across SITE Santa Fe and other venues in the city. Eshun commissioned new works from Edgar Arceneaux, Firelei Báez, Raven Chacon, Lotus L. Kang, and Cauleen Smith. Additional participating artists include John Akomfrah, Frank Bowling, Olafur Eliasson, Jeffrey Gibson, Nan Goldin, Delcy Morelos, Eamon Ore-Giron, Rose Simpson, and Sandra Vásquez de la Horra. Eshun stated that these practices share a sense that the world is continually reshaped by perception and imagination, inviting audiences to consider alternative ways of being.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Arte 2026 | TAREK EL-ARISS | Emptying the Jars of War, or How We Learned to Love Nature - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Tarek El-Ariss to Discuss War, Nature, and Water Politics at Biennale Arte 2026
articles.excerpt: Tarek El-Ariss will examine how crises alter perceptions of nature and reframe sustainability during a lecture at Biennale Arte 2026.
articles.content: Tarek El-Ariss is scheduled to speak at an event during Biennale Arte 2026 on November 21, 2026. Taking place at Teatro Piccolo Arsenale from 16:00 to 17:30, the lecture will be introduced and moderated by Rasha Salti. The session addresses how crises and wars not only damage the environment but also unsettle perceptions of nature. Drawing from everyday scenes such as saving water jars for bathing during wartime in Lebanon, the discussion traces longer histories and mythologies of water and greenery from the Garden of Eden to Greek and Islamic traditions, while focusing on the oasis as a recurring fantasy. The lecture posits that environmental practices do not necessarily emerge from ethical choices, often arising instead through habit, fear, or the quest for survival. Sustainability is reframed as a negotiation that interrogates the politics of purity and control to imagine alternative futures. Admission to the event is free until venue capacity is reached.

articles.originalTitle: FRIEDA EKOTTO | Resilience Against Value: Authored Practices of Repair in Otobong Nkanga and Ibrahim Mahama - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Frieda Ekotto to Deliver Lecture at Teatro Piccolo Arsenale
articles.excerpt: Frieda Ekotto will deliver a lecture examining the repair practices in the works of Otobong Nkanga and Ibrahim Mahama. The event takes place on November 20, 2026, at Teatro Piccolo Arsenale.
articles.content: Frieda Ekotto will present a lecture examining the gathering, wrapping, repairing, and regenerating actions central to the practices of Otobong Nkanga and Ibrahim Mahama. The event is scheduled for November 20, 2026, from 16:00 to 17:30 at Teatro Piccolo Arsenale. The discussion explores processes that redirect materials, labor, and time toward connections between land, body, and community that extraction seeks to disrupt. These actions form a resilience rooted in acts of refusal. By framing disobedience as the foundation of resilience, the lecture recasts the work of both artists as a sustained challenge to damaging value systems, pointing toward a relational model of authorship. Rasha Salti will introduce and moderate the session. Admission to the venue is free until capacity is reached.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Arte 2026 | ZIAD ANTAR | Bladder Diplomacy - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Ziad Antar Presents Bladder Diplomacy Lecture Performance at Biennale Arte 2026
articles.excerpt: Scheduled for Biennale Arte 2026, Bladder Diplomacy weaves together international diplomacy, agricultural habits in the eastern Mediterranean, and personal family stories through a satirical performance.
articles.content: La Biennale di Venezia hosts the lecture performance Bladder Diplomacy at Tese dei Soppalchi on 18 November 2026, running from 16:00 to 17:20. The event weaves stories of international diplomacy and the cultivation of potatoes and tomatoes in the eastern Mediterranean together with personal family narratives. The work examines radical interventions in the natural environment and nutritional habits introduced to the region by modernization and globalized agribusiness. Lebanese artists Ziad Antar, Hatem Imam, and Nayla Mabsout collaborate on the performance, drawing a satirical puzzle of malicious weeds, civil wars, and the resilience of indigenous seeds. The script is written by Ziad Antar, directed by Hatem Imam, and features video by Nayla Mabsout, with Ziad Antar and Nayla Mabsout performing. Visitors must hold a valid admission ticket to Biennale Arte 2026 in order to attend the scheduled event.

articles.originalTitle: Liverpool Biennial Announces Artist List and ‘Age of Magical Thinking’ Theme - ARTnews.com
articles.title: Liverpool Biennial Announces 2027 Theme and Artist Lineup
articles.excerpt: The 2027 Liverpool Biennial will run from June 5 to September 19 under the theme "The Age of Magical Thinking," inspired by Jean Piaget.
articles.content: The 2027 edition of the Liverpool Biennial is scheduled to run from June 5 through September 19 under the theme "The Age of Magical Thinking." According to a press release, the title draws upon psychologist Jean Piaget's identification of a childhood development period when the boundaries between reality and make-believe blur. Curated by Aimee Harrison and Lucía Sanromán, the exhibition will span multiple venues across North West England, including the Bluecoat, FACT Liverpool, Walker Art Gallery, Open Eye Gallery, Victoria Gallery & Museum, Liverpool Cathedral, and the Exhibition Research Laboratory at Liverpool John Moores University. The event will feature 25 artists and collectives. Highlights include a public art project in Williamson Square created by local young people alongside artist Harold Offeh, alongside new commissioned works by Francis Alÿs, Tania Candiani, and Laakkuluk Williamson. The participating artists include Ad Minoliti, Amalia Pica, Anya Paintsil, Charmaine Poh, Dor Guez, EBB.Global, Elias Nafaa, Hiroko Kubo, Immy Mali, Iván Argote, the vacuum cleaner, Wen Cheng Lee, Marilyn Boror Bor, Petrit Halilaj, Rineke Dijkstra, Robert Gabris, Ronak & Roza Moshtaghi, Ruth Ewan, Yarema Malashchuk, Roman Khimei, and Zohra Opoku.

articles.originalTitle: Yokohama Triennale announces title and theme for 2027 - ArtReview
articles.title: Yokohama Triennale Announces Title and Theme for 2027
articles.excerpt: The 2027 Yokohama Triennale, conceived by artistic directors Cosmin Costinaș and Inti Guerrero, will be titled "Whalefall: News and Rumours from the Ocean Floor."
articles.content: Conceived by artistic directors Cosmin Costinaș and Inti Guerrero, the 2027 Yokohama Triennale will be titled "Whalefall: News and Rumours from the Ocean Floor." The exhibition is scheduled to take place from April 23 to September 12 at the Yokohama Museum of Art. The theme of this edition builds upon two marine creatures and phenomena: the oarfish, whose rare appearances near the surface have historically been interpreted as disaster warnings in Japan, and the whale, which sinks to the ocean floor upon death to nourish an entire ecosystem. The Triennale uses these aquatic occurrences as a central metaphor. Examining ocean-based episodes in communication history, the exhibition will trace trajectories ranging from rumours spread by seafaring missionaries to the undersea cables powering the modern internet. Through a specifically commissioned architectural intervention by Tange Kenzō, the Yokohama Museum of Art will be transformed into the body of a whale.

articles.originalTitle: Loro Piana Celebrates Finest Cashmere, Stages Exhibition - WWD
articles.title: Loro Piana Stages Exhibition in New York and Awards Finest Cashmere Producers
articles.excerpt: Loro Piana presented the 2025 Cashmere of the Year Award at The Brant Foundation in New York and unveiled an immersive exhibition highlighting the brand's heritage and craftsmanship.
articles.content: Loro Piana hosted the 2025 Cashmere of the Year Award ceremony at The Brant Foundation in New York, celebrating fiber fineness reaching 12.89 microns. Inner Mongolian herders were recognized for producing exceptionally fine cashmere during the event, which also marked the opening of the Master of Cashmere exhibition detailing the brand's heritage and production methods. Company executives emphasized that the initiative honors the dedication of local herding communities and reinforces long-standing collaborative relationships in the region. The program aligns with broader sustainability and biodiversity efforts supported by the company in Mongolia. Additionally, the brand recently inaugurated an extensive knitwear manufacturing complex in the Piedmont region of Italy to consolidate major production stages within a single facility.

articles.originalTitle: This Belgian designer’s home is a ‘winterised’ take on California modernism - Wallpaper*
articles.title: Belgian Designer Adapts California Modernism for Her Countryside Home
articles.excerpt: Belgian interior architect Bieke Casteleyn adapted California midcentury modernism to her country's cooler climate while designing her family residence.
articles.content: Located in a flat countryside area in Belgium, the residence stands as a winterized interpretation of California modernism. Set on a single level, the home pairs warm wood tones with abundant natural light, featuring grey-green exterior stones chosen to blend with the landscape and a grass-covered flat roof. Inside, main living areas are separated from the private wing by a sweeping corridor framed by glass walls. The designer balanced extensive glazing and long sightlines by incorporating warm tones, tactile textures, and organic curves. Rather than fitting furniture into a pre-existing layout, the interior was designed around a collection of vintage pieces, family antiques, and collectible designs. Thoughtful architectural touches, such as a circular roof opening for a growing tree and a deck overlooking a pond, deepen the connection to the surrounding natural environment.

articles.originalTitle: 2026 Record Awards Winner: The Snake Building by C+S Architects - Architectural Record
articles.title: The Snake Building by C+S Architects Wins Record Award in Belgium
articles.excerpt: Located in a historic Belgian city on a former industrial site, the 29-unit Snake Building designed by C+S Architects has won a 2026 Record Award. The four-story development reinterprets traditional Flemish streetscapes.
articles.content: Situated in a historic Belgian city on a former industrial site, the four-story Snake Building designed by C+S Architects has won a 2026 Record Award. Rising from a J-shaped lot and containing 29 residential units, the multifamily housing project forms part of a master plan led by a2o Architekten. The massing comprises five gabled volumes separated by balcony gaps to break down the scale of a large housing block. The design features hand-laid long-format gray bricks and timber-framed windows. Hana Kassem praised the project's use of vernacular architectural language and tactile materials. A rear courtyard facilitates daylighting and ventilation for terraces, while a landscaped plaza with retail storefronts wraps around the street-facing elevations. Structural and MEP engineering were provided by Filip Van Den Voorde and Technieken respectively, with Altebra acting as fire safety consultant. Below grade, a garage accommodates resident parking.

articles.originalTitle: Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires – exhibition large print guide - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Constantinople to Istanbul: One City Shared by Two Empires
articles.excerpt: A Victoria and Albert Museum guide examines the rich history and art traditions of the city that maintained its strategic position across Roman, Byzantine, and Ottoman eras.
articles.content: Originally established as Nova Roma by Roman Emperor Constantine I in 330 CE, the city served as the center of the Byzantine Empire and later became the capital of the Ottoman Empire following its fall in 1453. Positioned at the meeting point of Asia and Europe, the settlement flourished through vital sea routes, attracting merchants, scholars, and pilgrims from diverse regions. According to the museum guide, monumental engineering feats such as the Theodosian Walls and the Aqueduct of Valens guaranteed the security of the metropolis across centuries. Transitioning through Roman paganism, Christianity, and majority Islamic traditions, the city's inhabitants fostered two distinct streams of art and design. The exhibition highlights this heritage through ivory plaques, manuscripts, cameos, and precious metalwork. While Byzantine Constantinople integrated sacred images into daily and political life, Ottoman culture often expressed reverence through intricate calligraphy. Historical objects, including restoration inscriptions and architectural fragments, document the enduring defensive and aesthetic ambitions of the imperial capital.

articles.originalTitle: jean nouvel’s shenzhen opera house takes shape on the waterfront, with completion set for 2028 - Designboom
articles.title: Jean Nouvel-Designed Shenzhen Opera House Scheduled for 2028 Completion
articles.excerpt: Designed by Ateliers Jean Nouvel, the Shenzhen Opera House is taking shape along the Shekou waterfront in China. Featuring a wave-inspired roof, the complex is expected to be completed by December 2028.
articles.content: Located in Dongjiaotou, Shekou, within Shenzhen, China, the Shenzhen Opera House rises on a site surrounded by water on three sides. Designed by the Paris-based team at Ateliers Jean Nouvel, the project features a sweeping curved roof evoking the movement of ocean waves. The complex brings together a 2,100-seat opera hall, an 1,800-seat concert hall, a 1,000-seat small opera hall, and a 500-seat multifunctional theater. Acoustic design is a priority, targeting a background noise rating below NR 15. Inside the main auditorium, the curves of the balconies and acoustic wall surfaces incorporate mother-of-pearl finishes to reference shifting water reflections. Construction incorporates specialized equipment, including welding and surveying robots, alongside digital design technologies. The main roof structure is scheduled for completion in 2027, with the overall project targeted for delivery in December 2028.

articles.originalTitle: Miami Beach: Highlights - Art Basel
articles.title: Art Basel Miami Beach Showcases Digital Art and Contemporary Masterpieces
articles.excerpt: Taking place at a cultural crossroads in the Americas, Art Basel Miami Beach unites voices in contemporary art while highlighting new frontiers in digital creations.
articles.content: Art Basel Miami Beach presents a program that unites prominent voices in contemporary art alongside innovative presentations. The regional art fair brings together modern masterpieces and emerging talent on a single platform. The Zero 10 platform, dedicated to digital-era art, returns with Generation, its largest presentation to date. Curated by Karen Archey and Eli Scheinman, the exhibition spans 19 projects and explores connections between digital technologies and traditional art forms. Encompassing algorithmic art, immersive environments, painting, sculpture, and textiles, the presentation highlights works by creators such as Sarah Meyohas, Jon Rafman, and Studio Drift. Refik Anadol's collaboration with the Yawanawá community transforms Amazonian artwork, music, and weather data into evolving digital imagery. Meanwhile, Harm van den Dorpel draws on historical geometric drawings to produce generative pieces that unfold in real time during the event.

articles.originalTitle: Italian Design Firm Henge Expands Into Tableware, Fragrances - WWD
articles.title: Italian Design Firm Henge Expands Into Tableware and Fragrances
articles.excerpt: Milan-based luxury furniture firm Henge has introduced its first collection of tableware, glassware, and home fragrances crafted from stone, glass, and metal.
articles.content: Italian luxury furniture maker Henge has expanded its portfolio into tableware, glassware, and home fragrances. The Milan-based company announced that its debut home collection relies on core materials such as stone, glass, and metal, featuring natural textures and hues. The collection includes Murano glass tumblers and a carafe designed by Ugo Cacciatori, alongside cast silver and gold trays by Yabu Pushelberg. Handcrafted in Carrara from Rouge Languedoc, Napoléon, and Gris Cévenol marbles, the Rever plates derive their name from the French word for dreaming. The brand also made its first foray into home fragrances with Henge Fragrance #34, named after its showroom at 34 Via della Spiga in Milan. The scent blends Calabrian bergamot, Sicilian lemon, and jasmine with notes of frankincense, Virginia tobacco, and Russian leather. This expansion aligns with an industry trend where high-end Italian design firms, including Molteni & C and Cassina, introduce smaller, more accessible design objects.

articles.originalTitle: About the Punk to Pop exhibition - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: V&A Museum Exhibition Explores Cultural Transformation from Punk to Pop
articles.excerpt: V&A South Kensington prepares to launch a comprehensive exhibition examining the explosion of music, art, and fashion between 1972 and 1985 in March 2027.
articles.content: Opening on 13 March 2027 at V&A South Kensington, the Punk to Pop exhibition re-examines the creative explosion across music, art, and fashion from 1972 to 1985. Spanning three acts and approximately 300 objects, the showcase traces a historical trajectory starting from glam rock and disco, moving through underground subcultures like punk, Goth, and New Romantics, and concluding with digital-era pop culture. Featuring prominent acts such as Sex Pistols, Grace Jones, Blondie, Joy Division, and Wham!, the exhibition demonstrates how self-determined artists responded to political turbulence and austerity. Highlighted items include album artwork by Jamie Reid, handwritten lyrics by Ian Curtis, Mick Jones's first guitar, and photographs by Andy Warhol. Through theatrical staging, fashion, and stage costumes, the multi-sensory presentation celebrates how music provided a platform for individuality, sexuality, and cultural experimentation during a transformative era.

articles.originalTitle: Miami Beach Director and Mendes Wood DM founders on the fair's bold new changes - Art Basel
articles.title: Art Basel Miami Beach Prepares Bold Structural Changes for 24th Edition
articles.excerpt: Marking its 24th year, Art Basel Miami Beach is implementing major revamps to its floor plan and gallery arrangements to improve navigation for collectors.
articles.content: Art Basel Miami Beach approaches its 24th edition with significant modifications to its gallery line-up and show floor plan. Fair Director Bridget Finn stated that feedback from exhibitors and selection committees prompted a more focused environment, allowing collectors to navigate the fair more easily and give presentations proper attention. The layout has transitioned from five plazas to a more symmetrical four-plaza configuration with redesigned entrances and sight lines. Gallery co-founders Matthew Wood and Pedro Mendes of Mendes Wood DM noted that the new layout recalls the spirit of discovery from their early participation. Mendes Wood DM is featuring Rosana Paulino's first bronze sculpture, Crisálida, originally created for the Brazil Pavilion at the 2026 Venice Biennale. Finn emphasized that success will be measured by the achievements of the participating galleries and the formation of new connections. The upcoming edition of Art Basel Miami Beach takes place from December 4 to 6, 2026.

articles.originalTitle: Edgar Degas | Promenade beside the Sea | L819 - The National Gallery, London
articles.title: Edgar Degas Painting Promenade beside the Sea at The National Gallery
articles.excerpt: Edgar Degas's early oil sketch Promenade beside the Sea, created around 1860 and depicting the Bay of Naples, is held at The National Gallery in London.
articles.content: Created around 1860 by Edgar Degas, Promenade beside the Sea stands as an early oil sketch exploring the recurrent theme of horses and riders. The artwork depicts an elegantly attired couple on horseback riding along a coastal route towards cliffs. A gentleman in black with a top hat and a lady sitting side-saddle in a dark riding habit make their way past coastal vegetation. The setting has been identified as the Bay of Naples, a location Degas visited during trips to see his Italian family. Open brushwork conveys the movement of the horses' gait, while impasto captures the energy of breaking waves. Measuring 22.5 by 32.5 centimeters, the oil on canvas is on long-term loan from the Gere Collection to The National Gallery in London, cataloged under inventory number L819. Evidence indicates the left-hand section derives from a notebook sketch housed in Paris. The composition reflects the artist's lifelong interest in movement and motion prior to the emergence of the Impressionist group.

articles.originalTitle: About the Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires exhibition - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: V&A Museum Explores Byzantine and Ottoman Legacy in Major Exhibition
articles.excerpt: The Victoria and Albert Museum is hosting Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires, an exhibition exploring 1,600 years of artistic production from AD 330 to 1922.
articles.content: V&A South Kensington in London is presenting Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires, an exhibition spanning the period from AD 330 to 1922. The exhibition examines the art and design traditions of both the Byzantine and Ottoman empires, highlighting their creative legacy that shaped the Mediterranean and beyond. Spread across four main sections, the exhibition features over 200 objects, including rare decorative arts, fine silks, textiles, ceramic tiles, mosaics, precious metalwork, jewelry, sculpture, architectural furnishings, manuscripts, and paintings. The first section, Roman Beginnings, explores the refounding of the city in AD 330 as the capital of the Roman Empire under Constantine the Great, focusing on its infrastructure and the Hippodrome. Heaven and Earth, the second section, explores how art and architecture served Christianity. Power and Reach examines how the Ottoman court projected authority through visual spectacle and luxury materials, while the final section, Life in the City, investigates the city's cosmopolitan character, religious coexistence, and 19th-century shifts in style. The exhibition remains open until 9 May 2027.

articles.originalTitle: Best Government/Public Building: Essex County Wynona Lipman Family Courthouse - Engineering News-Record
articles.title: Essex County Wynona Lipman Family Courthouse Wins Recognition
articles.excerpt: Built in Newark, the 266,000-square-foot, eight-story Essex County Wynona Lipman Family Courthouse consolidates previously dispersed family courts into a central location.
articles.content: Situated in Newark, the 266,000-square-foot, eight-story Essex County Wynona Lipman Family Courthouse consolidates previously dispersed family and children courts, probation services, and domestic violence units into a central urban location. The primary public entry is carved out under the upper floors to form a plaza as an extension of the streetscape. According to the submission, family courts require a de-escalating environment, addressed here by a multicolor art-glass two-story translucent screen on the public street wall and separate child-friendly playrooms in waiting areas. Constructing the massive complex in downtown Newark required meticulous coordination, including working within strict property lines, managing daily traffic flows, and minimizing disruptions to neighbors. The interior design divides spaces to separate hostile parties while accommodating sensitive zones, and integrates modern security with separate private entry points, holding cells, secure sallyports, and underground parking for judges. To counter unpredictable conditions, the project team relied on daily meetings and constant communication, allowing project managers, superintendents, and safety managers to address obstacles, coordinate daily tasks, and adapt in real time alongside cooperation with the city of Newark.

articles.originalTitle: Lunchtime Lectures: Curating Urushi Now: Contemporary Japanese Lacquer - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Victoria and Albert Museum Hosts Curator Talk on Contemporary Japanese Lacquer
articles.excerpt: The Victoria and Albert Museum hosted a curator talk and display exploring the research and collection process behind contemporary Japanese lacquer art.
articles.content: The Victoria and Albert Museum presented a talk exploring the research and travel process behind the Urushi Now: Contemporary Japanese Lacquer project. Led by curator Masami Yamada, the event detailed the initiative funded by the Art Fund and Hiroyuki Maki. Spanning from northern Japan's urushi lacquer forests to artist studios nationwide, the project brings together works by 41 living artists, ranging from Living National Treasures to emerging talents. Hosted in the Toshiba Gallery of Japanese Art, the display highlights how artists are rethinking traditional materials through contemporary techniques. The resulting display remains open to visitors in Room 45 until April 30, 2027. Curator Masami Yamada also authored an upcoming publication on contemporary Japanese craft scheduled for release in the spring of 2027.
